newsitem.title: ITALY: Somalis ask UN chief to probe Italian allegations.
newsitem.headline: Somalis ask UN chief to probe Italian allegations.

text.p: The head of the Somali community in Italy asked U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan on Friday to launch an inquiry into allegations that Rome's troops in Somalia engaged in torture and rape.

The allegations, based on photographs and interviews with Italian soldiers who served in Somalia as part of a multinational force from late 1992 to early 1994, have been published over the past few weeks in the news magazine Panorama.
Italy has opened inquiries into the allegations, which prompted the resignation of the commanding officers of the Italian force in Somalia, generals Bruno Loi and Carmine Fiore.

"Documentation of violence, torture and rape...by the Italian contingent of Operation Restore Hope has prompted four investigations in Italy," Fatuma Hagi Yassin, president of the Somali community, said in a letter to Annan.

"We ask you to begin an investigation to verify the accusations of criminal or, in any case, incorrect behaviour by military during Operation Restore Hope," said her letter, released at a news conference.

The letter suggested that an eventual U.N. inquiry should also cover behaviour of troops from other countries. Canadian and Belgian troops who served in Somalia are also alleged to have perpetrated abuses.
In a separate letter to Italian President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro, Yassin said those responsible "at all levels" should be rooted out.
The Panorama evidence includes photographs of what appeared to be the sexual assault of a young Somali woman by Italian soldiers using a military flare.
The army said on Friday it had suspended Sergeant Antonio Meligeni as a precautionary measure. Meligeni was one of the soliders pictured taking part in an alleged assault.
Another sergeant was suspended last week after he was identified in a Panorama photograph of an alleged case of torture.
Also on Friday, army general Nicolo Manca resigned in protest against what he called a "nauseating" campaign against the armed forces over the Somali affair.

At the news conference, Douglas Duale, lawyer for the Somali community in Italy, said a woman who claimed to have been raped had come forward and that he was trying to determine if she was the one in the photos.
Duale said 36 Somalis had come forward with accusations of torture, rape and other forms of violence by Italian soldiers during the international peace-keeping operation.
The Panorama allegations have caused deep shock in Italy, a former colonial power in Somalia which has taken pride in the role of its military in peacekeeping efforts abroad.
They coincide with Italian leadership of a multinational security force deployed in Albania ahead of elections there scheduled for next week.
Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta told parliament this week that a government-appointed commission would brook "no hesitation, no cover-ups and no delay" to get to the truth.
But he called for a sense of proportion in the scandal, saying the armed forces as a whole should not be demonised.
Italian army generals have hit back at the allegations, saying many of the accusations were false or exaggerated.
